title: Lost in Translation: Why Lower Bias Scores Don't Mean Fairer Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.20479v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Bias audits of multilingual language models usually compare a model's average stereotype score in English with its average in another language and read the difference as a difference in fairness. We ask how much of that difference is noise. Auditing ten open models in eight languages, we measure how far scores move when English test items are merely reworded, test every language shift item by item, and check that the test catches shifts we inject on purpose. In all 70 model-language pairs the stereotype score falls below its English level, and for Hindi, Korean and Swahili the drop clearly exceeds what rewording English produces; most of it comes from StereoSet items. Judging every translation, we find that imperfect ones drop more, but faithful translations alone drop nearly as much. Still, a lower average does not show that a model is fairer. translated_title: 翻译中的迷失：为什么更低的偏见分数并不意味着更公平的模型
translated_abstract: 多语言语言模型的偏见审计通常将模型在英语中的平均刻板印象分数与其在另一种语言中的平均分数进行比较，并将二者的差异解读为公平性上的差异。我们探究这种差异中有多少其实是噪声。我们审计了八个语言下的十个开源模型，测量当英语测试项仅仅被改写时分数的变动幅度，逐项检验每一次语言转换，并验证该测试能够捕捉我们故意注入的转换。在全部70个模型-语言对中，刻板印象分数均低于其英语水平，且印地语、韩语和斯瓦希里语的下降幅度明显超过改写英语所导致的下降；其中大部分下降来自StereoSet测试项。通过对每个翻译进行评判，我们发现不完美的翻译下降幅度更大，但即使只看忠实的翻译，也几乎出现同样程度的下降。尽管如此，更低的平均值并不能表明模型更公平：一个测试项的英语分数对其翻译后分数的预测能力远不如对其改写后分数的预测能力。
tldr: 本研究审计了10个开源模型在8种语言中的偏见表现，发现非英语语言下刻板印象分数的下降主要源于翻译缺陷与测量噪声，而非模型本身更公平，因为测试项的英语分数对其翻译后分数的预测能力远低于对改写后分数的预测能力。
en_tdlr: Auditing ten open models across eight languages, this paper shows that lower stereotype scores in non-English languages largely stem from translation imperfections and measurement noise rather than genuine fairness gains, as an item's English score predicts its translated score far less reliably than its reworded score.
